analysis.title: Cloud / Platform Engineer (Kubernetes, GCP, AWS)
analysis.fit_rationale: The candidate has strong infrastructure and automation experience, including AWS migration support, Python automation, and capacity/performance engineering. However, the role emphasizes Kubernetes, GCP, and AWS platform engineering with IaC (Terraform/CloudFormation) and CI/CD, which are not core to the candidate's professional evidence. AWS is at 'Advanced' project-level, GCP and Kubernetes are not listed, and Terraform/CloudFormation are absent. The candidate's strengths in Python, Linux, and cloud-adjacent work provide a foundation, but the gap in core platform engineering skills limits fit.
strengths: Expert-level Python and SQL/Oracle, with strong ETL and automation experience.
Professional experience supporting an AWS migration (G6 Hospitality).
Advanced AWS skills from a serverless lakehouse project (S3, Glue, Athena, Bedrock).
Strong capacity planning, performance engineering, and observability background (Dynatrace, CA APM, BMC TrueSight).
Experience with Linux-based environments and large-scale data migrations (Sabre).
gaps: No professional evidence of Kubernetes orchestration or containerized application deployment.
No GCP experience listed in the profile.
No hands-on experience with Terraform or CloudFormation (IaC tools).
No explicit CI/CD pipeline implementation experience.
AWS experience is project-level, not professional production deployment.
tailoring_plan: Tailor the resume to emphasize AWS migration support and any container-related coursework or projects. Add a skills section listing Kubernetes, GCP, Terraform, and CI/CD as 'familiar' or 'learning' if applicable. In the cover letter, highlight Python automation and Linux expertise, and express eagerness to learn Kubernetes and GCP. Quantify achievements in cloud cost optimization or scalability where possible.
